hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so a conv on 1->3 adds no useful path.
Edge 1->2 carries nothing when node 1 has no incoming edge.
A conv on 0->1 helps less when node 1's route to the output through edge 4 is already cut.
Replacing a removed direct input-to-output edge with a conv gives a much larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Adding a conv where the edge was none restores a path into the output, which gains more than swapping one op for another.
Replacing none with a conv gains more than replacing a stronger op.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip loses accuracy, whereas skip replacing none or pooling gains or is neutral.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 only gets input through node 1, so a conv on 2->3 matters less.
The skip already gives a good direct path, so upgrading it to a conv gains less than replacing none.
Downgrading a conv on the final edge to a skip costs accuracy, unlike replacing none or pooling.
